— Sahara Reporters (@SaharaReporters) October 30, 2026
Armed men have reportedly kidnapped Omoyele Sowore, the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), in Ekiti State.

The incident reportedly occurred on Friday, October 30, 2026, although details surrounding the circumstances of the alleged abduction remain unclear.

Sowore, a human rights activist, journalist and former presidential candidate, is yet to be heard from following the reported incident.

As of the time of filing this report, there has been no official statement from the police or the AAC regarding the alleged kidnapping.

Further details, including the location of the incident and the identity of those responsible, are still awaited.

AFCON To Return To Two-Year Cycle After CAF U-Turn by BlackViper(op): 3:12pm
The Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) will return to its traditional two-year cycle after a U-turn from the Confederation of African Football (Caf).

In December, Caf announced that the tournament would be held every four years instead, but that decision has been reversed after a review.

Under the new plans, the governing body was planning an African Nations League to replace Afcon as its biennial tournament, but acknowledged that it would take several years to generate the revenue required to become self-sufficient.

"The decision by the Executive Committee to reinstate the organisation of the Afcon every two years aims to advance, protect and promote the interests of African football and the 54 Caf Member Associations, as well as those of African players playing for clubs outside the continent," Caf president Patrice Motsepe said in a statement.

The biennial hosting of Afcon has long caused issues with the football calendar, with the vast majority of recent tournaments held midway through the European club season.

Fifa's expanded 32-team Club World Cup was held in June and July last year, which also forced Caf to opt for mid-season dates.

The next Afcon will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament, followed by editions in 2028, 2031 and 2033. There will be no tournament in 2030 because of the World Cup.

The dramatic 2025 Afcon final saw Senegal crowned champions before they were stripped of their title three months later in favour of Morocco.

https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cqn73pxx8vr5o

In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, 2026, and s...
item.content:encoded:
The Peoples Democratic Party in Ogun State has dismissed reports alleging that the name of its governorship candidate, Oladipupo Adebutu, was missing from the list of candidates released by the Independent National Electoral Commission.

The party described the reports as false and misleading, accusing those behind them of attempting to create confusion within its ranks ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

In a statement issued on Thursday, October 29, 2026, and signed by its State Publicity Secretary, Kayode Adebayo, the PDP said there was no official publication or update on INEC’s website confirming Adebutu’s purported exclusion.

The party also stated that INEC had not issued any official statement or held a press briefing announcing the alleged exclusion of Adebutu or the publication of a list containing the name of another individual identified as Patanmi from Gombe State.

The statement, titled “Re: Purported Exclusion of Hon. (Dr.) Oladipupo Adebutu from INEC List — A Fabrication by Political Jobbers,” described the report as an attempt by political opponents to undermine the PDP candidate.

“The said report is false, unfounded, unverified and a figment of the imagination of its mischievous authors,” the party said.

The PDP maintained that Adebutu remained its authentic candidate for the Ogun State governorship election, expressing confidence that his name would appear on the ballot in line with the relevant constitutional provisions, the Electoral Act and INEC guidelines.

The party urged its supporters, members and the general public to disregard the reports and remain focused on its political activities.

It added that the party remained united and committed to its preparations for the forthcoming election, insisting that the alleged controversy would not distract its members.

As of the time of the statement, the PDP said it had not seen any official INEC publication confirming the reported exclusion.

item.description:

She was, however, returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre after the court reserved ruling on her bail application till November 6.

Ogala, who is facing charges bordering on alleged cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor, expressed remorse before Justice...
item.content:encoded:
Nollywood actress Doris Ogala, on Friday, knelt down before a Federal High Court in Lagos to apologise to the court over her unruly behaviour during an earlier sitting.

She was, however, returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre after the court reserved ruling on her bail application till November 6.

Ogala, who is facing charges bordering on alleged cyberstalking, cyberbullying and attempted extortion of Pastor Chris Okafor, expressed remorse before Justice Akintayo Aluko, promising not to repeat the conduct that disrupted proceedings at the previous sitting.

The actress, who had been remanded at the correctional centre following her arraignment on Wednesday, personally appealed to the judge, saying she regretted her actions and never expected to find herself in prison custody.

She said, “I am very sorry, my Lord. I apologise for my bad behaviour. I have never been to prison before and I wasn’t expecting that I would do that.

“I regret my actions and I apologise to my Lord. I tender my apologies wholeheartedly. Sorry, this will never happen again going forward.”

Her apology followed the judge’s expression of displeasure over her unruly behaviour on Wednesday, after she was remanded.

Ogala allegedly shouted and sang in the courtroom, disrupting proceedings and forcing the court to rise.

Justice Aluko said her conduct prevented the court from hearing more than seven other cases scheduled for that day.

The judge said he had considered committing the actress for contempt on the day of the incident but decided against it, despite believing that her conduct warranted punishment.

He said, “She should have been given some form of imprisonment, right, on that day, but I kept my cool and I rose.”

The judge further said the actress could have received at least two months’ imprisonment for obstructing court proceedings.

Expressing his displeasure, Aluko said, “Why do you have to start shouting and start singing in the open court? You conducted yourself in a manner that forced the court to rise. That’s what you did, and it’s already recorded.”

He also faulted the defence counsel for failing to begin his address on the bail application by not acknowledging the incident and explaining the defendant’s conduct to the court.

The judge recalled that he had personally directed an accelerated consideration of the bail application, explaining that he had taken steps to ensure that it was heard within 48 hours.

He expressed disappointment that the Wednesday disruption occurred despite the court’s efforts to give the matter accelerated attention.

Ogala’s counsel, Marshal Abubakar, also apologised to the judge, describing the incident as regrettable and assuring the court that such conduct was not consistent with his client’s character.

He said he had known the defendant for some time and did not expect her to behave in that manner.


Following the apologies, the court proceeded to hear arguments on the bail application.

Moving the application, Abubakar urged the court to admit his client to bail, arguing that the prosecution had effectively acknowledged her entitlement to bail by proposing conditions for her release in its counter-affidavit.

He submitted that the prosecution’s position showed that it was not opposed to the defendant being released but was concerned about the conditions attached to her release.

According to him, where the prosecution accepts that a defendant may be admitted to bail, the court should exercise its discretion judicially and impose reasonable conditions.

He argued that bail conditions should not be unnecessarily restrictive, urging the judge to consider the circumstances of the case and the applicable provisions of the law.

The defence counsel also cited judicial authorities in support of his argument that bail conditions should be reasonable and should not undermine the right of an accused person to liberty pending trial.


However, the prosecution, led by Tolulope Mokolu, urged the court to impose stringent conditions on the actress, particularly in view of concerns about her activities on social media.

The prosecution argued that Ogala’s continued use of social media could negatively affect witnesses and potentially interfere with the administration of justice.

He maintained that although the defendant enjoyed the constitutional rights to freedom of speech and expression, such rights were not absolute and must be exercised within the limits of the law.


Mokolu therefore urged the court to restrict her contact with witnesses and their addresses and prevent her from making social media publications capable of influencing witnesses or undermining the proceedings.

The prosecution further argued that any breach of the proposed bail conditions should attract appropriate sanctions.

After listening to the submissions of both parties, Justice Aluko reserved ruling on the bail application till November 6, 2026.

Ogala was subsequently returned to the Kirikiri Correctional Centre, where she will remain pending the court’s decision on her bail application.

The actress was arraigned on Wednesday by the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation on three counts bordering on alleged cyberbullying, cyberstalking and attempted extortion involving Pastor Okafor.

Prosecution counsel, Tolulope Mokolu, alleged that Ogala committed the offences between September 2024 and March 2026.

Mokolu told the court that the actress allegedly published nude and intimate photographs of Okafor on her social media accounts without his consent, exposing him to embarrassment, emotional distress and reputational damage.

She pleaded not guilty to the charges.

In an interview with Ogala’s counsel, Marshal Abubakar, said he will petition the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, to withdraw the criminal charges against his client, describing the case as a private dispute between former lovers.

Abubakar disclosed this on Friday while reacting to the decision of the Federal High Court in Lagos to reserve ruling on Ogala’s bail application till November 6, 2026.

Speaking after the proceedings, Abubakar said he believed the prosecution of Ogala was an infringement on her fundamental rights, insisting that the dispute which led to the charges arose from a failed relationship.

He said, “I strongly believe that the arrest of Doris Ogala, the investigation as far as this matter is concerned, and the subsequent filing of charges against her are an affront to her fundamental rights.

“The subject matter that led to this entire transaction in this matter was purely a matter between a boyfriend and a girlfriend. Where former lovers fell apart, and one of the lovers felt cheated, and she reacted through the platform that she has.”

The lawyer stated that the state should not ordinarily involve itself in such a private dispute, adding that Nigerians had the right to express their grievances.

He said, “As far as I am concerned, these are private issues and private matters that the state ordinarily should not involve itself with. Nigerians have a fundamental right to express their grievances and express themselves in manners that they deem fit and appropriate.

“The idea of criminalising free speech in this country has been contemptuous. We will never shy away from condemning the idea behind having a law that seeks to, or has, a chilling effect on Nigerians as it relates to how they should express themselves in a democracy.”


Abubakar further said that individuals who felt defamed by another person’s statements should seek redress through civil proceedings rather than using law enforcement agencies to arrest and prosecute their critics.

According to him, democracy accommodates dissent and criticism, even where the expressions are considered offensive.

“Democracy accepts dissent. Democracy accepts even vulgar abuses where a person feels strongly defamed by the utterances of a person who has exercised his right under the law as it relates to their fundamental rights to express themselves.

“The natural remedy for such a person is to file a civil matter under the tort of defamation. If I feel strongly defamed by the utterances of a particular person, what I naturally would want to do is to go to court, where my integrity and reputation can be put on the line,” he said.


The lawyer maintained that approaching law enforcement agencies to arrest individuals over criticism or insults had no place in a democratic society.

He also called for the removal of provisions of the Cybercrimes Act which, according to him, criminalise free speech.

Abubakar recalled that in 2022, challenges were brought before the courts against provisions of the Cybercrimes Act 2015, particularly Section 24, which he said had been declared unconstitutional in two separate judgments for violating the right to freedom of expression and provisions of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights.

He said the National Assembly subsequently amended the Act in 2024 to address concerns surrounding the criminalisation of free speech.

However, he alleged that security agencies had continued to apply the law without adequately reflecting the amendments.

The lawyer accused some influential individuals and public officials of using law enforcement agencies to intimidate critics, arguing that such practices undermined democratic freedoms.

He said, “Today, when you insult somebody who is a man of means, or you insult a government official who has done something very bad, the same government official will simply approach the police and give them money to arrest and detain such an individual. In a democracy, this should never be.”

Asked whether he would formally challenge the prosecution, having appeared before the court, Abubakar said he intended to write directly to the Attorney-General and Minister of Justice, urging him to intervene.

He said, “It is also my honest belief that this matter should be discontinued and the charges withdrawn. In that regard, I will be filing an application to the Minister of Justice and the Attorney-General to withdraw this charge because it ought not to have been filed in the first place.”

He added that the request would be made in the interest of justice, insisting that the dispute should not proceed as a criminal case against a Nigerian citizen.

Katsina: 64 Students Hospitalised After Deworming Medication as Teachers Face Abuse Allegations

64 Katsina students hospitalised after taking deworming medication, teachers accused of beating pupils who complained of illness

At least 64 students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, Katsina State, have reportedly been hospitalised after developing complications following the administration of medication for schistosomiasis, a parasitic worm infection.

According to security analyst Zagazola Makama, the incident occurred on October 26, 2026, when several students began experiencing vomiting, dizziness and abdominal pain after taking the medication.

Some of the affected students were reportedly unconscious by the time they arrived at the hospital.

The students were taken to General Amadi Rimi Specialist Hospital in Batagarawa, Katsina General Hospital and Turai Yar'Adua Hospital for medical attention.


The report also alleged that some teachers physically assaulted students who complained of feeling unwell, accusing them of pretending to be sick rather than seeking medical assistance for them.

Makama called on the Katsina State Government and the Ministries of Education and Health to investigate the incident, including the type of medication administered, its dosage and whether proper medical supervision was provided.

He also urged authorities to investigate the allegations against the teachers and take appropriate action if they are found responsible.

item.content:encoded:
FIFA U-17 WWC: Flamingos Beat Mexico 2-1, Set Up Quarterfinal Clash With Venezuela

Nigeria’s Flamingos have reached the quarterfinals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 women’s World Cup after defeating Mexico 2-1 in Thursday’s round of 16 tie, completesports.com reports.

Oluebube Umejiaku put the Flamingos ahead late in the first half while Mary Dunstan doubled the lead with less than 20 minutes left in the second half.

Emily Delgado pulled a goal back for Mexico deep in added time but the Flamingos held on to advance to the last eight.

The Flamingos will now take on Venezuela in the quarterfinal on Sunday, November 1st. Venezuela reached the quarterfinal after edging out Germany 1-0.

Citlalli Reyes made the first attempt on goal just four minutes into the game but failed to find the back of the net.

Three minutes later Reyes went close again but to broke the deadlock for her side.

In the 20th minute the Flamingos had their first chance on goal but Oluwakemi Adegbuyi could not convert her chance, while Umejiaku also could not find the back of the net on 26 minutes.

With five minutes left in the first half Umejiaku put the Flamimgos 1-0 ahead as she took advantage of a poor interception by a Mexican player, dribbled her marker inside the box and fired past the keeper.

The Flamingos edged the early part of the second half and almost went 2-0 up on 48 minutes up Queen Joseph’s attempt was cleared away.

On the hour mark a dangerous corner kick from a Flamingos player deflected off a Mexican player but the keeper was quick to stop the ball from going in.

Some minutes later Flamingos continued to create scoring chances and were almost rewarded but Tosin Rafiu’s long lob was stopped from going in by the Mexican keeper.

Then in the 71st minute, Dunstan made it 2-0 as she volleyed into the back of the net after the keeper failed to properly punch away a cross into the box.

The goal was reviewed for a possible foul on a Mexican keeper in the build up to the goal but it was finally given.

With two minutes left a Mexico player Mia Urbano tried a long range strike but Flamingos keeper Jane Ijirigho tipped it against the bar.

But in the 10th minute of added time Delgado scored for Mexico as she controlled a poor clearance from a corner kick and fired a left-foot shot into the net.

The goal by Mexico turned out to be a consolation goal as the Flamingos held on to advance into the quarterfinals.

item.description:

Showunmi, who made the call in Makurdi, said Benue’s approximately 3.05 million registered voters represented significant electoral strength that could enhance the state’s voice in national political decisions if effectively mobilised thro...
item.content:encoded:
The National Convener of The Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi, has called for greater unity among political leaders and communities in Benue State, saying this would strengthen the state’s influence in national affairs.

Showunmi, who made the call in Makurdi, said Benue’s approximately 3.05 million registered voters represented significant electoral strength that could enhance the state’s voice in national political decisions if effectively mobilised through unity, responsible political participation and collective engagement.

He urged political leaders and communities across the Tiv, Idoma and Igede groups to foster cooperation and rise above political differences, noting that a united approach could strengthen efforts to address insecurity, promote development and advance the state’s interests.

Showunmi, who is also a member of the media and communications team of the APC 2027 presidential campaign, spoke during a visit to the state to assess public opinion on the administrations of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Hyacinth Alia ahead of the next general elections.

He said interactions with political stakeholders, women, youths and members of the Inter-Party Advisory Council indicated encouraging responses to the two administrations.

According to him, ongoing infrastructure projects, efforts to revive industries and initiatives to promote local production are among the developments that could stimulate economic activities in the state.

Also speaking, the State Coordinator of The Alternative Movement, Adai Edwin Adai, urged the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, and Governor Hyacinth Alia to embrace dialogue and reconciliation in the interest of peace and development in Benue State.

Adai expressed concern that prolonged political disagreements could heighten tensions and undermine peaceful political participation ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He called on the two leaders to prioritise the welfare of Benue residents and work together to address insecurity, unemployment and challenges affecting education, agriculture and economic development.

Adai cited former Senate Presidents David Mark and Iyorchia Ayu, alongside Akume, as examples of politicians who had maintained relationships and resolved differences through dialogue despite political disagreements.

He urged political leaders in the state to adopt a similar approach by putting aside their differences and prioritising the collective interests of Benue residents.

A Will can only be made by someone who is adjudged to be of sound mind at the time of making the Will.

And since he owns a lot of landed property, under Nigerian law landed property can only be transferred by a title document which can only be in written form.

It is clear that this young man was depressed and labouring under a huge psychological load.

I would humbly advise his family to carry out an autopsy on his body before he is buried to certify that there was no foul play at work.

His wife and children can still inherit his property if they apply for Letters of Administration, but it is a long process, much longer than would have been the case if he had simply prepared a written Will in the manner contemplated by the nation's laws on succession.

I don't know what exactly he did wrong and I don't want to speculate, but I pray his troubled soul finds rest.

As my Jewish friends say: "May his memory forever be a blessing"

item.content:encoded:
Fake Drugs: Metuh Demands Harsher Penalties, Slams Five-year Jail Term by ogugwa1992(op): 11:54am

– Tasks N’Assembly On Tougher Laws, Asset Forfeiture

An elder statesman and politician, Chief Olisa Metuh, has called for stiffer penalties for the production and distribution of fake drugs and adulterated consumer products, describing a five-year jail term or N5 million fine as grossly inadequate.

Metuh, who is the Director of Mobilisation and Organisation of the Renewed Hope Ambassadors (RHA), said the government must stop dealing with the malaise with kid gloves.

He was reacting to Wednesday’s conviction of a businessman, Innocent Okoye, by the Federal High Court in Abia State for producing and distributing fake Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Okoye was sentenced to five years’ imprisonment, with an option of N5 million fine.

Describing the sentence as a “mere slap on the wrist,” Metuh warned that such punishment could make counterfeiting and product adulteration a manageable business expense for unscrupulous manufacturers and distributors.

He said adulterated medicines, food, beverages, cosmetics and household products could cause serious illnesses, organ damage and preventable deaths, noting that unsuspecting Nigerians often bear the consequences of offences capable of affecting hundreds or thousands of people before detection.

“The law must respond with consequences that fit the crime,” Metuh said, arguing that the absence of direct physical confrontation between offenders and their victims does not make product counterfeiting any less dangerous than conventional violent crimes.

The lawyer urged the National Assembly to urgently review existing laws on drug counterfeiting, pharmaceutical adulteration and falsification of consumer products, with penalties reflecting the harm caused, offenders’ intentions, financial gains and degree of recklessness.

He called for substantially longer prison terms, including sentences comparable to those for grave violent crimes where offences result in death or serious injury, alongside fines proportionate to illicit profits and damage caused.

Metuh also advocated asset forfeiture, closure of offending facilities, compensation for victims, withdrawal of dangerous products from circulation and prosecution of corporate executives, manufacturers, importers and distributors who knowingly facilitate such crimes. He, however, stressed that tougher laws must be backed by swift prosecution and consistent enforcement.

“A five-year jail term or N5 million fine amounts to a mere slap on the wrist,” he said, insisting that such punishment must never become the price of doing business with human lives.

The Senate had in July 2026 passed for second reading the Counterfeit Medical Products, Fake Drugs and Unwholesome Processed Foods (Prohibition and Control) Bill, 2026. The proposed legislation prescribes a 15-year jail term upon conviction, asset forfeiture, compensation for victims and stronger enforcement powers for the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

item.title: 'We Know How AI-generated Images Entered the Voters Register' - Bayode - Politics
item.description:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has traced the appearance of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs in its preliminary register of voters to irregularities allegedly introduced by some registration officers who had access to its registration system.

INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed this on Friday during an appearance on Arise Television, explaining that some registration officers across...
item.content:encoded:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has traced the appearance of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs in its preliminary register of voters to irregularities allegedly introduced by some registration officers who had access to its registration system.

INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed this on Friday during an appearance on Arise Television, explaining that some registration officers across the country used their login details to introduce questionable records into the database.

He said the commission discovered the irregularities through its Automated Biometric Identification System, which was used to examine the registration records.

“We have registration officers on the field. And these registration officers, they have login details to log into the system.

“So what we have found is that some of these registration officers, not all of them now, some of them across the states nationwide, they’ve done different things to bring these irregularities onto the register,” Bayode said.

He explained that while some of the photographs were generated using artificial intelligence, others resulted from poor registration procedures.

“Some of these pictures are AI-generated. Some of them not AI-generated, but very bad registration. And this thing got into the register by the registration officers and because they have access to register people,” he said.

Bayode added that INEC had identified the records and understood how some of the irregularities occurred, but could not explain why the officers involved had introduced them.

“When the ABIS was run on the system, we saw these people. We know what they did. We know how they did it. But honestly, I don’t know why,” he added.

The ICT director said the commission had been working to clean up the register even before publishing the preliminary version, adding that it was under pressure to complete the exercise within the statutory 90-day period.

The disclosure follows public concerns over suspicious photographs and other irregularities discovered after INEC uploaded its preliminary register of voters to its website on October 26.

As previously reported by The PUNCH, screenshots circulated on social media showed photographs suspected to have been generated using AI attached to voter records in parts of Edo State.

Other concerns included alleged duplicate entries and complaints by some registered voters that their details were missing from the online register.

INEC had earlier said the online version was the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas nationwide between October 9 and 15 for the Display, Claims and Objections exercise.

In a statement on October 27, the commission said some questionable records had been identified and flagged during the physical display, adding that it had commenced a review and corrective action.

It also stressed that the published register was not the final certified version and that the online release did not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities.

INEC is expected to complete its verification, adjudication and data-cleanup processes before certifying the final Register of Voters on December 15, 2026.

Victor Osimhen & Stefanie Welcome Baby Girl, Liora Audrey by kidap(op): 9:04am

Galatasaray and Nigeria striker Victor Osimhen and his partner Stefanie Kim Ladewig have officially welcomed their second child into the world—a healthy baby girl named Liora Audrey.

The Turkish Süper Lig champions confirmed the joyful news on Thursday via their official channels, offering a warm message to the growing Osimhen family.

Official Announcement
“Our Football A Team player Victor Osimhen and Stefanie have welcomed a baby girl into the world. We congratulate the couple Victor and Stefanie; we wish their newborn baby Liora Audrey a long, healthy, and happy life!”

Key Family & Pitch Details

Second Child: Liora Audrey is the couple’s second daughter, joining big sister Hailey, who was born in October 2022.
Relief After Incident: The joyous arrival comes weeks after Stefanie escaped unharmed following a minor three-vehicle traffic accident in Istanbul.
Blistering Form: Osimhen continues his red-hot streak for Galatasaray, sitting as joint-top scorer in the Turkish Süper Lig with 8 goals in 7 league games after scoring a brace against rivals Fenerbahçe earlier this week.
Squad Duty: Osimhen remained in Istanbul on Thursday to support his family before rejoining the squad ahead of Galatasaray’s fixture against Konyaspor.

Source: https://cms.sureodds.ng/congratulations-victor-osimhen-stefanie-welcome-baby-girl-liora-audrey/

item.title: APC Rejects Court Ruling, Insists Uzodimma Is Senatorial Candidate - Politics
item.description:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Imo State has rejected a Federal High Court ruling recognising former governor Rochas Okorocha as its candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains its flagbearer.

item.content:encoded:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Imo State has rejected a Federal High Court ruling recognising former governor Rochas Okorocha as its candidate for Imo West Senatorial District in the 2027 general elections, insisting that Governor Hope Uzodimma remains its flagbearer.

The party said Uzodimma emerged victorious in its senatorial primary with the overwhelming support of its members, adding that its legal department would study the court’s decision before determining its next course of action[/i

[i]The position was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by the APC State Publicity Secretary, Onwuasoanya Jones, following the ruling by Justice Obiora Egwuatu of the Federal High Court, Abuja.

The court had ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish Okorocha’s name as the APC candidate for the senatorial district ahead of the January 16, 2027 election.

It also directed Uzodimma to stop presenting himself as the party’s candidate for the election

However, the APC maintained that the governor remained its duly nominated candidate, citing the outcome of the party’s primary election.

“The Party wishes to state without any confusion that His Excellency Distinguished Senator Hope Uzodimma, CON, remains the candidate of our Party for Imo West Senatorial District, having won the primaries of our great Party with the overwhelming support of the majority of our Party members,” the statement said.

The party said it would examine the court’s decision before taking further action on the dispute.

“The Party’s legal department shall study the outcome of a legal intervention in this matter and act accordingly,” it added.

The APC also called on its members and supporters to remain committed to the party’s political objectives and work towards securing victories across Imo State in the 2027 elections.

The dispute stems from the APC senatorial primary held on May 18, 2026, in which Uzodimma was declared the winner with 230,464 votes, while Okorocha was credited with 1,098 votes, according to the results recognised by INEC.

Dissatisfied with the outcome, Okorocha approached the court to challenge the process and the recognition of Uzodimma as the party’s candidate for the district.

In its ruling on Thursday, the court held that Okorocha was the lawful winner of the primary and ordered the APC to submit his name to INEC for publication as its candidate.

The court also questioned inconsistencies in documents submitted by the party in support of Uzodimma’s nomination.

item.description:
YOU DON'T HAVE TO BE RICH TO BE A BLESSING TO OTHERS

Have you ever wondered how many people have benefited from your existence?

item.content:encoded:
YOU DON'T HAVE TO BE RICH TO BE A BLESSING TO OTHERS

Have you ever wondered how many people have benefited from your existence?

How many people have smiled because of something you did? How many people have found relief because you showed up for them? How many people have had their burdens reduced because you were willing to help?

Sometimes, we think we need to become wealthy before we can help others. We think we need to occupy an influential position before we can make a difference.

But that is not true.

You don't have to be rich to be generous. You don't have to be famous to be impactful. You don't need a prominent position to make someone's life better.

A student who helps another student understand a difficult subject is doing something valuable.

A neighbour who shares food with a struggling family is doing something valuable.

An employer who pays workers their wages promptly and treats them with dignity is doing something valuable.

A husband who makes life easier for his wife, and a wife who supports her husband through difficult times, are doing something valuable.

A person who listens to someone going through emotional difficulties, offers encouragement, or helps someone find their feet is doing something valuable.

These may appear to be ordinary acts, but when done sincerely for the sake of Allah, they can become acts of worship.

The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught us that even simple acts of goodness should never be underestimated.

He said:

“Do not consider any act of kindness insignificant.”

— Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim 2626.

Think about that!

Sometimes, a kind word can prevent someone from giving up. A little financial assistance can help a struggling student remain in school. A simple visit can make someone battling illness feel remembered. A sincere apology can restore a broken relationship.

You may consider these things too small to matter, but you never know how much they mean to the person receiving them.

Allah also reminds us:

“And do good; indeed, Allah loves those who do good.”

— Qur'an 2:195.

So, don't wait until you become a millionaire before helping someone. Don't wait until you become a professor before sharing your knowledge. Don't wait until you occupy a political or religious position before serving humanity.

Start with what you have.

Use your knowledge to educate someone. Use your money to support someone. Use your influence to open doors for others. Use your position to protect those who are vulnerable. Use your words to encourage rather than destroy.

And above all, never become the reason another person's life becomes unnecessarily difficult.

A beautiful life is not measured only by what you accumulate, but also by how many lives become better because you lived.

May Allah make us beneficial to others, accept our little acts of kindness, and make us a source of relief, happiness and goodness wherever we find ourselves.

item.content:encoded:
LESSONS WE MUST LEARN

1. Never compromise your faith to please people.

These young men refused to exchange their belief in Allah for societal acceptance. Today, many people compromise their religious values because they want to fit in, impress friends, secure relationships or gain social approval.

Remember, people's approval is temporary, but your relationship with Allah is far more valuable.

2. Your environment and friendships matter.

These young men strengthened one another in faith. They did not encourage one another towards wrongdoing.

Look carefully at the people around you. Do your friends bring you closer to Allah or gradually pull you away from Him?

3. You are never too young to be serious about Islam.

Allah specifically described them as young men:

إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ آمَنُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى

“Indeed, they were young men who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance.” (Qur'an 18:13)

You do not have to wait until you are old, married, wealthy or retired before taking your faith seriously.

4. Sometimes protecting your faith requires difficult decisions.

The young men left their familiar environment because remaining there threatened their faith. Sometimes, you may need to walk away from certain friendships, environments, relationships or opportunities to protect your relationship with Allah.

5. Never underestimate the power of du'a and trust in Allah.

When they found themselves in difficulty, they turned to Allah. They did not have all the answers, but they knew where to seek help.

Their story reminds us that when we sincerely turn to Allah, we should never underestimate His ability to provide a way forward.

item.content:encoded:
Tinubu To Present 2027 Budget Before December 31 – Minister by Dapagun(op): 7:13am
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is expected to present Nigeria’s 2027 budget proposal to the National Assembly before the end of 2026, the Minister of State for Budget, Dr Doris Uzoka-Anite, has disclosed.

Uzoka-Anite made this known on Wednesday while speaking with State House correspondents after the Federal Executive Council (FEC) meeting presided over by President Tinubu at the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

The minister explained that the Federal Government was already working on the preparation of the 2027 budget, with plans to submit the proposal to the National Assembly before the end of the year.

“We are working on the 2027 budget, and our intention is to present it before the end of the year,” she said.

However, the minister did not disclose the specific date President Tinubu would formally present the budget to lawmakers.

The proposed 2027 budget is expected to outline the Federal Government’s spending priorities, revenue projections and economic plans for the coming fiscal year.

Meanwhile, the Budget Office of the Federation has introduced stricter documentation requirements for ministries, departments and agencies (MDAs) seeking personnel cost allocations in the 2027 budget.

In a circular dated September 4, 2026, the Budget Office directed all MDAs to submit their personnel cost proposals alongside copies of their respective establishment Acts.

item.title: FBI Offers $5,000 Reward For Emuobosan Emmanuella Hall - Crime
item.description:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of a Nigerian woman, Emuobosan Emmanuella Hall, who allegedly failed to report to prison to begin serving an eight-year sentence for her involvement in a romance fraud scheme in the United States.

The US Department of Justice announced the reward on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, following a federal grand jury indictment accusing Hall of failing to report to the Bureau of...
item.content:encoded:
The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) has announced a $5,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of a Nigerian woman, Emuobosan Emmanuella Hall, who allegedly failed to report to prison to begin serving an eight-year sentence for her involvement in a romance fraud scheme in the United States.

The US Department of Justice announced the reward on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, following a federal grand jury indictment accusing Hall of failing to report to the Bureau of Prisons as directed by the court.

Hall, 46, is a Nigerian citizen and permanent resident of the United States who previously lived in Atlanta, Georgia. She is currently wanted by US authorities, and an arrest warrant has been issued against her.

According to the Department of Justice, Hall was sentenced to 96 months in prison in January 2026 after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit mail and wire fraud, as well as conspiracy to commit money laundering.

She was ordered to report to her designated correctional facility on or before March 25, 2026, but failed to comply with the court’s directive.

Investigators said information retrieved from Hall’s electronic monitoring device showed that her last known location was Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on March 24, 2026. The device reportedly stopped transmitting data at the airport.

Hall had earlier informed her probation officer that she intended to travel to Minnesota, where she was expected to serve her prison sentence. However, airline records reportedly showed that she did not board the flight.

The FBI is appealing to members of the public to provide any information that could help investigators locate and arrest her. The agency is offering $5,000 for information that leads to her arrest.

Anyone with relevant information has been advised to contact the FBI through its telephone line, 1-800-CALL-FBI, or submit a tip through the agency’s official online reporting platform.

How The Romance Fraud Scheme Operated
Court records showed that Hall previously admitted to participating in a romance fraud scheme that targeted victims, mostly older women, across different parts of the United States.

Members of the criminal network allegedly created fake identities and presented themselves as military generals, philanthropists or successful entrepreneurs living abroad.

They reportedly established relationships with victims through social media platforms, including Facebook and Instagram, before persuading them to send money under false pretences.

The victims were allegedly told that the money was needed for charitable projects, medical expenses for sick relatives or other purported emergencies.

Investigators said Hall and her co-defendant, Kenneth G. Akpieyi, used a company known as Le Beau Monde LLC to facilitate the scheme.

Hall allegedly deposited money obtained from victims into bank accounts operated in the company’s name before transferring the funds to other financial institutions, including banks outside the United States.

The court held Hall responsible for losses totalling $851,207 suffered by victims of the scheme.

Her co-defendant, Akpieyi, was sentenced to 25 years in prison in January 2026 for his role in the criminal operation.

Hall Faces Additional Prison Sentence
Beyond the eight-year sentence imposed for the romance fraud and money laundering offences, Hall could face up to 10 additional years in prison if convicted of the new charge of failing to report to serve her sentence.

The latest charge is separate from the offences for which she had already been sentenced.

The US Department of Justice, however, emphasised that the allegations contained in the new indictment remain accusations that must be proven beyond a reasonable doubt in court.

The FBI’s reward offer is part of efforts by US law enforcement authorities to locate Hall and bring her before the court to answer the latest charge.

Bill For Federal College Of Education, Umuobom Scales Second Reading In Reps by Gurunews(op): 6:59am
The bill seeking to establish the Federal College of Education, Umuobom, Imo State, has passed second reading in the House of Representatives.

The bill, sponsored by the member representing Ideato North/South Federal Constituency, Ikenga Ugochinyere, seeks to upgrade the Imo State College of Education, Umuobom, to a federal institution.

The proposed legislation scaled second reading at plenary on Thursday, a major milestone in efforts to expand access to quality teacher education and boost educational development in Imo State.

The bill, titled: “A Bill for an Act to Establish Federal College of Education, Umuobom, Imo State, and for Related Matters,” provides legal framework for the institution’s establishment, administration, academic programmes, infrastructure, research and staffing.

Under the proposed law, the college would operate as a corporate body with powers to acquire and manage properties, while its academic programmes and standards would be supervised by the Federal Ministry of Education through the National Commission for Colleges of Education.

Leading debate on its general principles, Ugochinyere said the bill seeks to strengthen capacity for learning, improve teacher training and advance the education sector through academic and research programmes.

He said the initiative underscores his commitment to educational development and attracting federal institutions to his constituency, with potential to create jobs, stimulate economic activities and expand access to higher education for youths in Ideato and neighbouring communities.

According to him, the upgrade will enhance the institution’s capacity to produce qualified teachers to improve educational standards in Imo and Nigeria at large.

The passage at second reading paves way for further legislative processes, including committee consideration.

When put to voice vote by the Speaker who presided over the session, the bill was passed and referred to the relevant committee for further legislative action.

item.title: Lagos Court Denies KC Luxury Bail, Orders Speedy Trial - Crime
item.description:
Justice Musa Kakaki of the Federal High Court in Lagos on Wednesday refused to grant bail to businessman and social media influencer Afolabi Michael Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, over alleged 184.5kg cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

The judge held that the defence had failed to establish special circumstances to warrant bail on medical grounds, insisting that the application lacked sufficient evidence to justify the defendant’s release.

The jud...
item.content:encoded:
Justice Musa Kakaki of the Federal High Court in Lagos on Wednesday refused to grant bail to businessman and social media influencer Afolabi Michael Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, over alleged 184.5kg cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

The judge held that the defence had failed to establish special circumstances to warrant bail on medical grounds, insisting that the application lacked sufficient evidence to justify the defendant’s release.

The judge further held that there was no medical certificate to warrant the court granting him bail.

“There is no medical certificate to warrant the court to grant him bail,” Kakaki ruled.

“If there is a special medical need for the first defendant, where a suspect claims an illness, an expert in the field would have given an explanation,” he said.

Kakaki, however, directed the Ikoyi Custodial Centre to grant Kazeem unrestricted access to doctors and medical experts for the treatment of any health condition.

The judge also ordered an accelerated hearing of the case, adjourning it until November 2, 2026, for the commencement of the trial.

At the last proceedings on Friday, Kazeem was brought to the court premises in an ambulance while receiving oxygen.

His counsel, Emefo Etudo, had urged the court to grant him bail to enable him to receive specialised medical treatment at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital.

Etudo argued that Kazeem’s health had deteriorated, particularly following the collapse of his lungs, which he said was disclosed by the Police Hospital, Falomo.

Opposing the application, prosecution counsel, Abu Ibrahim, argued that the medical evidence presented by the defence did not sufficiently justify the defendant’s release.

“Your Lordship looked at the application. The ailment is the same. It is the same asthma. But maybe it has become acute; the character and the ailment are the same,” Ibrahim said.

He added that the defence had not presented a medical document from LUTH showing that the hospital could not manage Kazeem’s condition.

When the case was called on Wednesday, a correctional officer from the Ikoyi Custodial Centre, Adeleye Akin, informed the court that Kazeem was still at the Police Hospital in Falomo.

Delivering his ruling, Kakaki said he had considered the bail application, the court records and the submissions of counsel on both sides.

The judge held that an applicant seeking bail must provide sufficient and cogent evidence to establish why the court should grant the request.

He also reviewed the medical evidence previously presented by the defence, including exhibits AK5, AK6 and AK8, which he said contained photographs of an individual lying on a hospital bed receiving treatment.

Kakaki recalled that in his ruling delivered on October 2, 2026, the court had noted a medical officer’s recommendation that Kazeem be assessed by a consultant respiratory physician or pulmonologist to evaluate his condition, optimise his treatment and prevent further acute episodes.

The judge said the recommendation did not establish that the defendant was suffering from an untreated illness.

He said, “Having gone through the records of the court and compared the ruling of October 2, 2026, I hereby discountenance all the exhibits.”

Addressing the defence’s argument that Kazeem needed specialised treatment at LUTH, Kakaki questioned the claim that the defendant could not be treated in a Nigerian hospital when the same application sought his release to enable him to receive treatment at the teaching hospital.

“Is it not ironic that the facility he said he cannot be treated in is the same LUTH he wants him to go to for specialised treatment?”

The judge also said the defence had failed to demonstrate any change in circumstances to justify a fresh bail application.

“However, changes in the circumstances were not disclosed.”

He recalled that on October 16, 2026, the court had ordered that Kazeem be remanded in a custodial centre.

“There is an inability to show special circumstances to warrant bail. I hereby discountenance it in the present application,” he said.

Kakaki further held that a claim of illness requiring specialist treatment should be supported by an expert’s assessment explaining the defendant’s condition.

“There was nothing stopping the Correctional Centre from calling an expert to attend to the first defendant, or using the first defendant’s doctor if he had one,” the judge said.

Refusing the application, Kakaki said, “The application is not granted; bail is refused to the first defendant. The case will proceed to an accelerated hearing.

“Where there is any health issue, the Correctional Centre shall give unfettered access to a doctor or expert for his treatment.”

Kazeem is standing trial alongside Boniface Freeman Ochoche Sule and Ikechukwu Ekugo Patriarch over alleged 184.5kg cocaine trafficking and money laundering.

The case was adjourned until November 2, 2026, for the commencement of the trial.

item.content:encoded:
Nigeria Women’s Football League champions Edo Queens have petitioned the Confederation of African Football (CAF), seeking to overturn their 3-2 extra-time defeat to Ghanaian champions Ampem Darkoa Ladies in the disputed final of the 2026 WAFU-B Women’s Champions League

In a petition dated after Thursday’s encounter, Edo Queens asked CAF to declare the continuation of the final, played on 29 October, null and void, citing alleged irregularities in the venue change, match arrangements and eligibility of players.

The Nigerian club also urged the continental governing body to suspend confirmation of the regional qualification slot for the CAF Women’s Champions League pending the determination of its complaint.

The fresh protest follows a contentious sequence of decisions that overturned Edo Queens’ initial victory in the regional final and gave both teams another opportunity to contest the title.

How Ampem Darkoa Won
Ampem Darkoa secured the WAFU-B title after defeating Edo Queens 3-2 following extra time in the rescheduled conclusion to the final.
The encounter followed the original meeting between the sides on 5 September in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, which ended 2-2 after 90 minutes.

Edo Queens subsequently won the penalty shoot-out 4-1 and initially appeared to have secured the regional championship and qualification for the continental competition.
However, Ampem Darkoa challenged the outcome, prompting CAF’s Organising Committee to rule on 26 September that the penalty shoot-out had no sporting effect.

The decision, subsequently upheld by the CAF Appeal Board on 16 October, directed that the match resume from the beginning of extra time with the score still at 2-2.

When play eventually continued on Thursday, Ampem Darkoa struck the decisive blow just two minutes into extra time to secure the 3-2 victory.

The Ghanaian champions thereby claimed the WAFU-B title and the zone’s qualification place for the 2026 CAF Women’s Champions League.

The triumph marks Ampem Darkoa’s return to the continental competition for the second time in their history, having previously featured in 2023 in Côte d’Ivoire.

item.content:encoded:
2027:If they kidnap our children, I will enter the bush with them—Presidential candidate Peter Obi vows to personally join rescue efforts if elected President

Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has vowed to take a hands-on approach to insecurity, saying he would personally join efforts to rescue Nigerians abducted by criminals if elected president in 2027.

Speaking at a town hall meeting in Enugu State on Thursday, Obi said Nigeria needed a president who would be active, accountable and directly involved in tackling the country’s challenges.

“If there is a general bush, I will be in that bush with them,” he declared.

“As President of Nigeria, I will unite Nigeria. As President of Nigeria, I will secure Nigeria. We will deal with insecurity. I will not be president and somebody will k+dnap our children; we will enter the bush together.”


Obi, who has been touring different states ahead of the 2027 elections, said Nigerians were battling hunger, unemployment and insecurity.

“Today, our country is suffering. Today, people are hungry. Our children do not have employment. Today, Nigeria is not secured,” he said.

He also challenged President Bola Tinubu to tour the country and explain his administration’s performance, including how borrowed funds have been spent.

“Our President must come and account for three years he’s been in office. He cannot stay in Abuja, and want us to vote for him. No! This job requires energy, requires travel,” Obi said.

“As President of Nigeria, we will put emergency on corruption. People must stop stealing public money. Public money must be used for public good,”

he said.

Obi urged Nigerians not to support him based on ethnicity, insisting, “Don’t vote for me, because I’m an Igbo man. Please, I’m asking for your vote because I’m the most qualified to be President of Nigeria.”

item.content:encoded:
The Federal Capital Territory Police Command has arrested a Deputy Superintendent of Corps with the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Onoja Samuel, for allegedly firing shots into the air during a confrontation with traders at a market in the Kubwa area of Abuja.

According to the police, Samuel had gone to the market armed with a pistol following reports that some traders had assaulted his wife.

In a statement on Wednesday, the FCT Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, said operatives attached to the Kubwa Police Division were promptly deployed to the scene and arrested the suspect after disarming him.

“On 25th October, 2026, at about 1:50 pm, a distress call was received at Kubwa Police Division reporting that an unidentified man, armed with a pistol, was firing sporadically into the air at a market in Kubwa, Abuja.

“Upon receipt of the report, Police operatives attached to Kubwa Division were promptly deployed to the scene. Following concerted efforts, the suspect was successfully disarmed and arrested.

“Preliminary investigations identified the suspect as one Onoja Samuel, a Deputy Superintendent of Corps with the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps.

“Further findings revealed that the suspect had gone to the market armed with a pistol following reports that some traders had assaulted his wife. During an ensuing argument with the traders, he fired several shots into the air, ” Adeh said.

The police spokesperson said a CZ pistol and 17 rounds of live 9mm ammunition were recovered from the suspect during his arrest.

She added that the NSCDC officer remained in police custody and would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations.

The Commissioner of Police in the FCT, Ahmed Sanusi, urged personnel of sister security agencies to exercise restraint and notify the police divisions responsible for areas where they intend to conduct authorised operations.

“Operatives of sister security agencies are urged to exercise restraint and notify the Police Divisions responsible for the areas in which they intend to conduct sanctioned operations within the FCT, to ensure proper coordination and prevent avoidable clashes,” he said.

item.content:encoded:
It's a breaking news, binance is hacked and 6 billion USD stolen.

Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has said that about $6.3bn in funds have been stolen in a “security incident” that looks to be the biggest crypto heist in history.

The world’s largest crypto exchange said on Thursday that it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals and that about $3bn in funds had been frozen following the apparent hacking.

Binance said an initial investigation suggested that a hacker had been able to make unauthorised transactions after gaining access to an engineer’s compromised laptop.

The company said it would cover all losses, adding that user funds were “safe”.

“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” Binance said in a statement to Al Jazeera.

“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.”

The company added that it would share a “detailed” technical post-mortem once investigations were complete.

Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder and largest shareholder, said earlier that the exchange appeared to have been hacked.

TRM, a blockchain intelligence firm, said in a report that it assessed with “high confidence” that the attack was carried out by North Korea’s hacking unit TraderTraitor, which investigators have linked to the Lazarus Group.
Ari Redbord, TRM’s global head of policy, described the attack as “unprecedented” and a “watershed”.

“When North Korea steals at this scale, the money funds weapons proliferation and other destabilising activity. That makes this a global security issue, not just a crypto theft,” Redbord told Al Jazeera.

The price of Bitcoin, the world’s most popular cryptocurrency, fell about 5 percent following the heist, dropping below $77,000.

“Binance is one of the largest centralised exchanges, and so a blow to confidence in them risks shocking confidence to many retail investors, which could dampen prices of crypto assets,” Sean Foley, an expert in crypto markets at Macquarie University in Sydney, told Al Jazeera.

Foley said the attack highlighted the risks of centralised exchanges and could spur more traders to use decentralised alternatives.

“Any assets held at a centralised exchange are only as safe as the exchange itself, and the larger the exchange’s holdings, the larger a target it becomes,” Foley said.

The Binance hacking dwarfs the previous record for a crypto theft, set in 2025 when North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group carried out a $1.5bn heist on Bybit.

Cybercriminals stole $2.87bn in crypto assets in nearly 150 hacking incidents in 2025, according to the 2026 Crypto Crime Report produced by TRM.

Binance, founded in China by Zhao in 2017, has about $155bn in assets under management, more than any other exchange, according to CoinMarketCap.

item.content:encoded:
UPTH RESPONDS TO VIRAL VIDEO, DEFENDS HOSPITAL SERVICES

Previous thread
https://www.nairaland.com/8773746/man-alleges-upth-denied-brother

The University of Port Harcourt Teaching Hospital (UPTH) has dismissed allegations in a viral video concerning its services, defending the availability of medical equipment while acknowledging challenges relating to electricity supply and staff shortages.

In a press release dated October 29, 2026, the hospital's Public Relations Officer, Mr. Kem Daniel-Elebiga, and Head of the SERVICOM Unit, Mr. Efere Azubalu, said the Accident and Emergency Department had no record identifying the patient featured in the video. The management also dismissed claims that a sphygmomanometer, used to measure blood pressure, was unavailable, insisting that decisions on medical procedures rested with qualified physicians.

On electricity supply, the hospital said power availability had improved following efforts by its Chief Medical Director, Professor Chituru Godwill Orluwene, to secure its inclusion in the Federal Government's Energising Education Off-Grid Solar Project at the University of Port Harcourt. However, it acknowledged that weather-related fluctuations and rehabilitation works sometimes caused temporary power interruptions, with critical areas given priority before full supply was restored.

The management also acknowledged manpower shortages, noting that the Federal Government was working to recruit more health workers. It explained that recruitment required institutional verification and compliance with established procedures, adding that the hospital was following due process to address its staffing gaps.

Reaffirming its commitment to healthcare delivery, training and research, UPTH urged journalists, partners and members of the public to verify information and engage the management whenever they had concerns. The hospital assured the public of its readiness to respond to inquiries and its commitment to providing professional and quality healthcare services.

item.content:encoded:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has been discharged from hospital and is "doing well" following his collapse at the club's training ground.

Kompany, 40, was rushed to hospital last Friday after taking ill as he watched the club's second team train.

The cause has been identified as meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

"Given the circumstances, he's doing well," Max Eberl, the club's board member for sports, told German broadcaster ARD on Wednesday.

"He was discharged from the hospital today. That is the biggest and best news for all of us."

No timeline has been set for Kompany's return and Bayern said on Saturday that it would be a matter of "weeks, not days" until the former Manchester City defender returned to the dugout.

English assistant coach Aaron Danks has taken over in Kompany's absence and oversaw a 3-1 win at Freiburg on Sunday.

Kompany had been nursing a virus in the days before his collapse and missed some team training sessions.

The Belgian missed a pre-match news conference prior to Bayern's Champions League game against Arsenal last Tuesday, but was subsequently on the touchline for the match on Wednesday.

"It's a meningeal irritation that caused this incident on Friday. He will now rest and take medication," said Eberl, speaking before Bayern's German Cup tie against Magdeburg.

"I am very confident that he will be back on the touchline, operating at 100% very soon."


Current leaders Bayern face title rivals Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

lexylaw40:
The “president-elect” saw in Obi's presidential bid, a good chance to reduce the winning chances of the presidential candidate of the PDP, Atiku Abubakar.

The governorship candidate of the Labour Party (LP) in Oyo State, Tawfiq Akinwale, [/b]on Wednesday [b]stated that the “President-elect” Bola Tinubu asked popular economist, Prof Pat Utomi to step down for Peter Obi in the buildup to the 2023 general elections.

Akinwale made this revelation while he appeared as a guest on a radio programme on 101.7 YES FM, Ibadan, Oyo State, while alleging that Obi received campaign funds from Utomi, whom he described as Tinubu's "son."

The LP aspirant, who spoke in Yoruba language, said "In the buildup to the 2023 elections, Obi who had purchased the nomination form of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), suddenly announced his exit from the party.

"Initially, Pat Utomi had secured the LP's presidential ticket, but when Peter Obi said he resigned from the PDP and joined the LP. Bola Tinubu, a master political strategist, quickly told Utomi, that everyone knows to be his son to step down for Obi.

"The “president-elect” saw in Obi's presidential bid, a good chance to reduce the winning chances of the presidential candidate of the PDP, Atiku Abubakar.

"What Peter Obi didn't know is much more that what he knows, he started collecting campaign funds from Utomi, while Tinubu was giving the money to Utomi.

"This went on until Obi's presidential campaign got to a stage it went beyond target. Obi was used without him knowing," Akinwale said after announcing his departure from the party.

Obi defected to the LP after resigning his membership of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and also withdrawing from the presidential race under the party.

The former governor consequently joined the race for the party’s presidential ticket, while Professor Pat Utomi, in June 2022 stepped down for him to emerge as the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, LP, unopposed in Asaba, Delta State.

item.content:encoded:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has cleared former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Ali Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 general elections, subject to the outcomes of pending court cases.

However, the commission rejected a petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who sought a review of his exclusion from the list of candidates.

A source at INEC disclosed the decisions to Daily Trust after the commission’s meeting on Thursday, saying it received 69 petitions from political parties over the omission of candidates for governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections.

According to the source, approximately 36 petitions were successful, while the remaining requests were rejected. However, the commission was still awaiting final figures from its legal department, which was preparing an official statement on the decisions.

“We received a total of 69 petitions from political parties. Some of them were successful, I think about 36, and the rest didn’t succeed,” the source said.

On Pantami’s candidacy, the source confirmed that INEC had cleared the former minister, who is seeking to contest the governorship election in Gombe State.

“Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said.

The official, however, noted that pending litigation could still affect the final status of the candidates.

Regarding Gwarzo, the source said the commission had no objection to his candidacy but stressed that its position remained subject to the court’s final decision.

“Because of the court case, the court may rule otherwise. So his approval is subject to whatever the court finally decides,” the source said.

The source added that INEC had no objection to either candidate contesting the election, provided the legal issues were resolved in their favour.

The commission, however, rejected Adebutu’s petition challenging his exclusion from the Ogun State governorship candidates’ list.

“He did not succeed,” the source said.

The decisions followed complaints by candidates and political parties after INEC omitted some names from its lists ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Pantami and Gwarzo were among the prominent governorship aspirants whose names were missing from the list published by the commission in October.

INEC had attributed the omissions to alleged non-compliance with provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 requiring political parties to submit their membership registers.

The commission said its position was based on a September 24, 2026, Supreme Court judgment affirming the constitutionality of Section 77(5) to (7) of the Electoral Act, which makes the submission of party membership registers mandatory.

Gwarzo subsequently approached the court to challenge the omission of his name and that of his running mate, Rabiu Mustapha, from the list of NDC governorship candidates in Kano State.

In an originating summons dated October 20, 2026, he asked the court to declare their exclusion unlawful and compel INEC to recognise them as the party’s governorship candidate and running mate.

Pantami’s candidacy has also been the subject of litigation, with the INEC source indicating that a court proceeding was expected on Friday.

Meanwhile, Adebutu had challenged his exclusion from the final list of governorship candidates in Ogun State, maintaining that he remained a registered PDP member and had complied with the party’s membership registration requirements.

INEC is expected to issue a formal statement detailing the outcome of its review of the petitions.

item.content:encoded:
Tinubu, Yayi Get Massive Support at City Boy Movement Rally in Ogun

…Ojeleye mobilises 2,000 to 3,000 supporters in Obafemi Owode

Members of the City Boy Movement in Obafemi Owode Local Government Area of Ogun State on Thursday turned out in large numbers to mobilise support for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, Senator Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates ahead of the forthcoming elections.

Our correspondent reports that the rally, held at All Saints School, Owode Egba, with over 3,000 supporters and members of the ruling APC in the state.

While speaking on the rationale behind the rally, the Obafemi Owode Local Government Coordinator of the movement, Hon. Abimbola Ojeleye, said the chapter was the first among Ogun State’s 20 local government areas to organise a mega rally of this nature.

She said the initiative was aimed at educating residents, particularly youths, about the forthcoming elections and encouraging their participation in the political process.

Ojeleye explained that the decision to organise the rally was informed by her assessment of the Tinubu administration’s performance and her desire to bring information about its programmes and the movement’s empowerment initiatives closer to residents.

Her words “When I sat down and looked at everything, I told my leaders that in my local government, I wanted to do this to tell my people and our youth about our progress".

She added that the rally was also intended to strengthen the movement’s ongoing registration exercise and mobilise grassroots support for Tinubu, Yayi and other APC candidates.

On the preparations for the event, Ojeleye acknowledged the support of the movement’s leadership, ward coordinators, women leaders and other grassroots supporters, who helped mobilise residents across communities.

“When I presented the idea to my leaders, they fully embraced it and supported us to go into the towns, houses and villages to mobilise the youths,” she said.

While expressing satisfaction with the turnout, she urged residents to participate actively in the forthcoming elections.

Also speaking, the Ogun Central Senatorial Coordinator of the City Boy Movement, Ambassador Lekan Egbetola Olalekan, urged coordinators in other local government areas to emulate the initiative by organising similar rallies and engagement programmes.

Egbetola described the rally as an example of grassroots mobilisation, urging other coordinators to take the lead in engaging residents and strengthening support for the movement.

“This is a particular example for other local government coordinators to see the need and take the lead,” he said.

He added that the turnout should encourage coordinators and their representatives to intensify mobilisation efforts in their respective areas.

On the funding of the rally, Egbetola disclosed that Ojeleye personally sponsored the event, sourcing financial support through her contacts, ward coordinators, women leaders and other individuals who believed in the movement.

He explained that the movement’s contribution was the empowerment package scheduled for distribution to beneficiaries at the event.

According to him, the initiative highlighted the importance of personal commitment and collective support in organising grassroots political activities.

Egbetola also appealed to residents of the South-West to support Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing student loans, road infrastructure, empowerment programmes and grassroots development as reasons for continuing the administration.

He called for similar support for Senator Adeola and other APC candidates, adding that the movement would sustain its mobilisation efforts ahead of the elections.

Dignitaries at the rally included Alhaji Mustafa Eruobodo, former Executive Chairman of Obafemi Owode Local Government; Ambassador Abeeb White, Deputy State Coordinator of the City Boy Movement; Comrade Salaudeen Muhammad, Secretary of the Ogun Central Senatorial Coordination; Alhaja Ogunyemi Fatimah Oluwayemisi, Director of Welfare, City Boy Movement, Ogun Central; and Hon. Gbenro Olasoju, Ward Chairman, Obada Oko.

item.description:
Apple has acknowledged some of its iPhone Duo handsets have developed problems with their screens, just days after the highly-anticipated smartphone went on sale.

Photos posted on social media show lines that appeared on the screens of the technology giant's first ever foldable device, which has a starting price of £1,999 ($2,668) in the UK.

Apple said it was aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of the phones and urged affected users to contac...
item.content:encoded:
Apple has acknowledged some of its iPhone Duo handsets have developed problems with their screens, just days after the highly-anticipated smartphone went on sale.

Photos posted on social media show lines that appeared on the screens of the technology giant's first ever foldable device, which has a starting price of £1,999 ($2,668) in the UK.

Apple said it was aware of "an issue impacting the inner display on a small number" of the phones and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement.

The Duo's launch, which attracted crowds at Apple stores around the world last week, is an attempt to reinvigorate the brand's device range and challenge the foldable phones made by rivals.

Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen's centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device.

An iPhone Duo user, Justin Lokos, posted an image of a device with lines across the right side of the display and later uploaded a picture of a new handset alongside the broken one, thanking an Apple store in New York for its help .

The extent of the issue remains unclear. Apple did not say how many devices were affected, while some images showing faulty devices may have been created using AI.

Francisco Jeronimo, technology analyst at market research firm IDC, said that meant some caution was needed before drawing conclusions about the whole production run

But he added the early reports of issues also showed "that even a company with Apple's engineering resources and supply chain discipline faces a steep learning curve in foldables".

Premium product

The Duo's 7.6-inch (19.3cm) inner display is held together by a central hinge - a complex piece of engineering that has resulted in similar flaws in folding devices made by some of Apple's competitors.

It is Apple's most expensive iPhone ever, costing up to £3,199 for the most well-equipped models.

Jeronimo said because Apple had positioned the Duo as a "premium alternative" to established foldables, "how it handles this first-generation issue will shape buyer confidence in the category well beyond its own sales".
