item.content:encoded:
Jubril A. Gawat @Mr_JAGs

UPDATE ON THE ONGOING REHABILITATION OF BONNY CAMP – OZUMBA MBADIWE - ADMIRALTY INTERSECTION ALONG ETI-OSA – LEKKI – EPE EXPRESSWAY

The Lagos State Special Adviser, Office of Infrastructure, Engr Olufemi Daramola paid an inspection visit to the ongoing rehabilitation of the Bonny Camp – Ozumba Mbadiwe - Admiralty Intersection along Eti-Osa – Lekki – Epe Expressway.

The visit was aimed at assessing the progress of work and monitoring the ongoing rehabilitation project.

SO FAR,

- Rehabilitation works are ongoing at a critical section of Ozumba Mbadiwe Road, between Adetokunbo Ademola Intersection and Samuel Manuwa Junction, along the Epe-bound carriageway.

- The contractor is fully active on site, and the construction works is progressing steadily as scheduled.

- The earthworks at this section have been completed, with stabilized crushed stone base and Geotextile material to prevent filtration of water from the pavement surface in place.

- At the time of the inspection, sand bedding was being laid in preparation for the installation of interlocking paving stones

- The adoption of the Paving Stones as the pavement surface is intended to address the route’s highwater table, climate-related conditions, and abuse by overloaded articulated trucks.

TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT

- The Traffic Management Plan was also reviewed during the inspection, and it was observed to be functioning effectively, ensuring smooth traffic flow and minimising disruption to motorists along the project corridor.

- The public’s support, patience, and understanding of the temporary traffic arrangements were acknowledged, while motorists’ compliance with the traffic management measures was commended.

NEXT STEP:

- The rehabilitation of this critical section is scheduled for completion by the end of November 2026. Upon completion, the contractor will temporarily demobilise from the site to minimise traffic disruptions and ensure smoother movement for motorists during the Yuletide season.

item.title: NAFDAC Destroys ₦8 Billion Fake Products In North-Central - Health
item.description:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has destroyed fake, adulterated, expired and banned products valued at more than N8bn seized across North-Central Nigeria.

The agency said most of the confiscated items were banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and small containers of less than 200ml.

Speaking at the destruction exercise in Lafia, Nasarawa State, on Thursday, the Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye, said the p...
item.content:encoded:
The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control has destroyed fake, adulterated, expired and banned products valued at more than N8bn seized across North-Central Nigeria.

The agency said most of the confiscated items were banned alcoholic beverages packaged in sachets and small containers of less than 200ml.

Speaking at the destruction exercise in Lafia, Nasarawa State, on Thursday, the Director-General of NAFDAC, Prof Mojisola Adeyeye, said the products were seized from manufacturing facilities, shops, markets and motor parks across the zone.

Adeyeye, represented by a Deputy Director of NAFDAC in the zone, Joseph Edor, said the ban on alcoholic beverages in sachets and glass bottles below 200ml was aimed at curbing their abuse, particularly among young people and schoolchildren.

According to her, the products’ affordability, availability and portability made them easily accessible for misuse.

She said, “Research has shown that early exposure to alcohol affects the brain and other vital organs such as the liver and kidneys.

“It stymies the brain, resulting in mental retardation, brain damage, poor performance of pupils in school, low productivity and several types of illnesses.”

Adeyeye said the ban and subsequent enforcement operations were prompted by concerns over alcohol abuse, addiction and its adverse health effects.

She added that other seized items included expired, counterfeit and unwholesome food products, medicines and cosmetics.

“It is in the course of carrying out these activities that this heap of unwholesome, banned, fake and adulterated products worth about eight billion naira was confiscated from manufacturing outfits, sales outlets, markets and motor parks.

“The bulk of the products in that pile are predominantly banned alcoholic beverages in low volumes of less than 200ml (20cl),” she emphasised.


The NAFDAC boss commended other law enforcement agencies and stakeholders for supporting the agency’s operations through intelligence sharing and security assistance.

Also speaking, the Nasarawa State Coordinator of NAFDAC, Dr Gyani Stephen, said the destruction was intended to protect public health rather than hurt businesses or individuals.

He warned traders involved in the sale of counterfeit and banned products to desist, saying the agency would take action against those who violated the law.

In a goodwill message, the Nasarawa State Commander of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency, Daniel Saidu, represented by Yakubu Awoh, commended NAFDAC for its efforts to remove expired and fake medicines from circulation.


He warned that allowing such dangerous products into the market could endanger millions of people and harm their mental health.

However, they said that when they tried to decorate the place the owners blocked them and said that the governor said that the place is only for the use of school childre...
item.content:encoded:
Some NDC members had posted videos and made posts to say that they wanted to hold a townhall meeting at Opara Square but were denied the use of the square. They said that they decided to use Amadeo Event Centre and had paid three million for the hall and five hundred thousand for the space outside the hall weeks ago. However, they said that when they tried to decorate the place the owners blocked them and said that the governor said that the place is only for the use of school children.

*PRESS RELEASE FROM AMADEO EVENT CENTRE:*

Statement on the Viral Video Concerning the Booking of AMADEO EVENT CENTRE

​Our attention has been drawn to viral videos circulating on social media claiming that the Management of Amadeo Event Centre prevented the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC) from using our facility for a booked event. This claim is false. We set out the facts below:

​On October 7, 2026, Dr Sabastine Chuks Ezeh (the Client), Registrar of the Nigeria Institute of Healthcare Givers and Medical Social Work Practitioners (hereinafter known as the Association), made a booking. In the Terms and Conditions of the Facility, the Client stated the rental was for a "National Meeting and Conference". The Conference was scheduled for October 15, 2026.

*2)*​On October 13, 2026, the Client wrote a "LETTER OF CANCELLATION AND REQUEST FOR REFUND", on the headed paper of the Association, requesting that the event be cancelled and the deposit refunded. He later withdrew the cancellation on the grounds that the Association wanted to postpone, rather than cancel.

*3)*​On October 23, 2026, the Client confirmed October 29, 2026, and we agreed that decoration would start on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

*4)* On the morning of October 28, 2026, the decoration materials that were brought were for a political party and had nothing to do with the Association. This clearly violated the contract for use of the place that we signed with the Client.

*5)* Clause 17 of the Terms and Conditions of Use of the Facility, which the Client signed, provides for the Right to Stop an Activity and reserves the right of Management to put a stop to any activity, meeting, or event not properly or reasonably conducted in line with the provisions of the terms and conditions or regulatory practices. It was on the basis of this violation that the Client was notified of the rescission of the right of use.

*6)* Upon receiving the notice of cancellation, Enugu State NDC officials and candidates entered our premises with security details. We were taken aback by the change of the client from the Association to an NDC political rally.

*7)* Despite the contractual violation, we allowed the event to proceed to forestall a breach of peace, after the organizers informed us it would now be used as a youth town hall meeting with Mr. Peter Obi.

Our position

*1)*​No political party booked our facility. Our only booking for October 29, 2026, was with the Nigeria Institute of Healthcare Givers and Medical Social Work Practitioners for a "National Meeting and Conference".

*2)* ​Amadeo Event Centre is a non-partisan venue. Our policy from inception has been to decline the use of our facilities for political purposes.

*3)* We did not request or seek police to deter the event. Rather, the policemen seen in trending videos were escorts for some of the political aspirants who came to the Event Centre after receiving the notice of cancellation.

*4)* At no point was the Enugu State Government (ENSG) part of this conversation. Management received no instruction, directly or indirectly, from any government official as this was purely a contractual matter.

*5)* This whole event has been distorted and viewed through a partisan perspective because of the current political season.

*6)* Amadeo Event Centre remains a venue for peaceful, lawful gatherings, including academic, social, religious, and corporate events.

MANAGEMENT

item.content:encoded:
New Delhi, Oct 29 (PTI) Police have arrested three Nigeria nationals and a Delhi resident for alleged drug trafficking and recovered 417 grams of MDMA (commonly referred to as Ecstasy) and 105 grams of cocaine, estimated to be worth Rs 1.5 crore in total, an official said on Thursday.

The accused were allegedly procuring, storing and supplying narcotic substances through a network of associates, and involved in wholesale and retail distribution, police said.

The arrestees have been identified as Nigeria nationals Nnamdi Osita alias Johan Peter (46), Victor Ocaforo (33) and Obinna Mike Ernest (32), and Attar Singh, alias Lucky (23). The three foreign nationals and Singh were allegedly residing in outer-west Delhi’s Nilothi area, a senior officer said.

“On September 25, a police team received information that Peter was supplying cocaine and MDMA across Delhi-NCR and would deliver narcotics near Shukar Bazar Road in Chander Vihar,” the officer said.

Acting on the tip-off, the team reached the spot and apprehended Peter and his two associates, Ocaforo and Ernest, after they allegedly attempted to flee into a nearby building.

During searches, the team recovered 55 grams and 301 grams of MDMA from Peter and Ocaforo, respectively, while 105 grams of cocaine was seized from Ernest.

The officer said during interrogation, Peter and Ernest allegedly disclosed their links with Singh, following which he was arrested from his residence in Nilothi. Police recovered another 61 grams of MDMA from his possession.

A case was registered in this connection at Crime Branch police station under provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, and Section 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, was subsequently added after the three foreigners failed to produce valid documents authorising their stay in India.

“Peter had come to India in 2013 on a tourist visa and was overstaying. Ernest arrived in 2016 on a business visa, while Ocaforo came in 2020 on a medical visa. All three were allegedly overstaying in the country,” the officer said.

Police also cited previous NDPS cases involving the three foreign nationals in Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Delhi and Haryana. Singh allegedly came into contact with them while procuring drugs for personal consumption and later began supplying them to other users for profit, police said.

Further investigation is underway to identify other persons linked with the alleged racket

item.content:encoded:
154 Students Recover After Suspected Bilharzia Drug Reaction In Katsina by Glimpsetv(op): 4:52pm On Oct 29
A total of 154 students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa in Katsina State reportedly fell ill after taking Praziquantel tablets during a school-based bilharzia treatment campaign on October 26, 2026.

Shortly after the medication was administered, many of the students began experiencing symptoms such as vomiting, dizziness, and abdominal pain. They were quickly rushed to health facilities, including General Amadi Rimi Specialist Hospital and Katsina General Hospital.

In a viral video from the scene, several of the students can be seen lying on the floor outside the school building while adults move around trying to attend to them.
According to the Katsina State Police, all the affected students have now fully recovered. They have been discharged from the hospitals and reunited with their families. No deaths were recorded.

The incident has raised serious concerns about the way the medication was administered. The state government is currently investigating possible issues related to dosage, medical screening of the students before the treatment, and the timing of the exercise.

Parents are also calling for stricter supervision and better safety measures during school health programmes to prevent a repeat of such incidents.

Re: 154 Students Recover After Suspected Bilharzia Drug Reaction In Katsina by omojeesu(m): 6:11am

Were they diagnosed to have any disease needing praziquantel?

Praziquantel is an anthelmintic (anti-worm) medication used to treat infections caused by parasitic flatworms, including blood flukes (schistosomes) and liver or intestinal flukes. [1] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610), [2] (https://www.vinmec.com/eng/blog/how-to-take-praziquantel-en), [3] (https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/drugs/19042-praziquantel-tablets)

Main Human Uses

• Schistosomiasis (Snail Fever / Bilharzia): Treats urinary and intestinal infections caused by Schistosoma (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F0215t0&q=Schistosoma) species (S. mansoni, S. haematobium, S. japonicum, S. mekongi), and is the primary treatment recommended by the World Health Organization. [1] (https://www.efda.gov.et/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Praziquantel-Tablets-600-mg_MACLEODS-PHARMACEUTICAL-LIMITED.pdf), [2] (https://www.vinmec.com/eng/blog/how-to-take-praziquantel-en), [3] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610)
• Liver Flukes (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F02lw7s&q=Liver+Flukes): Treats clonorchiasis (Chinese liver fluke, Clonorchis sinensis) and opisthorchiasis (Southeast Asian liver fluke, Opisthorchis viverrini). [1] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610)
• Other Flukes & Tapeworms (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F0214zx&q=Tapeworms): Treats various intestinal flukes (Fasciolopsis buski (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fg%2F120mc1_q&q=Fasciolopsis+buski), Heterophyes heterophyes (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F09gh6bz&q=Heterophyes+heterophyes)), lung flukes (Paragonimus westermani (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F06v46m&q=Paragonimus+westermani)), certain tapeworm infections (Diphyllobothrium latum, Hymenolepis nana), and neurocysticercosis (when used alongside anti-inflammatory steroids). [1] (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3780935/), [2] (https://www.vinmec.com/eng/blog/how-to-take-praziquantel-en)

How It Works

Praziquantel paralyzes the muscles of the parasitic worms by disrupting their calcium ion balance. This causes the worms to detach from blood vessel walls or tissues, after which they are either destroyed by the body's immune system or passed out in the stool. [1] (

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yl8jjZ3b54U), [2] (https://www.facebook.com/dijitalveteriner/posts/praziquantel-doesnt-simply-kill-the-parasiteit-disrupts-its-calcium-balance-and-/1671816351615400/), [3] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610)

Important Safety & Administration Notes

• Prescription Only: You must obtain this medication through a healthcare provider. [1] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610)
• Administration: Tablets should generally be swallowed whole with water during a meal to avoid its bitter taste (which can trigger gagging or vomiting). [1] (https://reference.medscape.com/drug/biltricide-praziquantel-342666), [2] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610)
• Veterinary Use: Praziquantel is also widely used by veterinarians to treat tapeworms (https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F0214zx&q=tapeworms) and other parasites in dogs, cats, and livestock (often sold under brand names like Biltricide, Droncit, or Drontal). [1] (https://vcahospitals.com/know-your-pet/praziquantel), [2] (https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/drugs/19042-praziquantel-tablets)
If you are asking for a specific person or pet, let me know:
• Who the medication is for (adult, child, or animal)
• What specific infection or symptoms you are trying to treat
I can share more tailored details about dosage or safety precautions.

Re: 154 Students Recover After Suspected Bilharzia Drug Reaction In Katsina by omojeesu(m): 6:14am

Did they get parental consent?

SIDE EFFECTS OF PRAZIQUANTEL
Side effects happen for two main reasons: direct effects of the drug or your immune system reacting to the dying parasites. Most mild side effects start soon after taking a dose and go away within 24 hours. [1] (https://incitefulmed.com/resources/questions/what-are-praziquantel-side-effects/)

Common Side Effects

• Digestive issues: Abdominal pain, stomach discomfort, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea.
• Nervous system: Headache, dizziness, drowsiness, and general fatigue.
• General feelings: Low energy, malaise (feeling unwell), mild fever, or sweating.
• Skin: Itching, rash, or hives. [1] (https://www.webmd.com/drugs/praziquantel-biltricide), [2] (https://www.apollopharmacy.in/salt/praziquantel), [3] (https://incitefulmed.com/resources/questions/what-are-praziquantel-side-effects/)

Serious Side Effects (Seek Medical Care Immediately)

• Severe allergic reactions: Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing. [1] (https://www.webmd.com/drugs/praziquantel-biltricide)
• Neurological changes: Seizures, confusion, or severe disorientation (especially if you have undiagnosed cysts in the central nervous system). [1] (https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/drugs/19042-praziquantel-tablets), [2] (https://www.webmd.com/drugs/praziquantel-biltricide)
• Heart rhythm changes: Fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat, or feeling faint. [1] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610), [2] (https://www.apollopharmacy.in/salt/praziquantel)
• Intense immune response: In heavy parasite infections (like schistosomiasis), the sudden death of worms can trigger high fever, severe headache, or worsening neurological symptoms as your body clears the debris. [1] (https://www.drugs.com/sfx/praziquantel-side-effects.html), [2] (https://www.webmd.com/drugs/praziquantel-biltricide)

Tips to Reduce Side Effects

• Take with food: Swallow the tablets whole during a solid meal or snack with a full glass of water.
• Do not chew: The pills have a very bitter taste that can trigger gagging or vomiting if broken or chewed in the mouth.
• Avoid driving: Do not drive or operate machinery while taking the medication and for 24 hours after your last dose, as it can cause dizziness or drowsiness. [1] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610), [2] (https://incitefulmed.com/resources/questions/what-are-praziquantel-side-effects/)
You can read more about safety and administration on the Cleveland Clinic Guide to Praziquantel or the Mayo Clinic Praziquantel Overview. [1] (https://www.mayoclinic.org/drugs-supplements/praziquantel-oral-route/description/drg-20065610), [2] (https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/drugs/19042-praziquantel-tablets)

item.content:encoded:
Okorocha Breaks Silence After Court Victory: ‘Presidency Tired of Nonsense’ by Kingzjayzee(op): 4:45pm On Oct 29
Former Imo State Governor, Rochas Okorocha, has reacted to the Federal High Court judgment which ordered Governor Hope Uzodimma to stop parading himself as the All Progressives Congress, APC, candidate for Imo West Senatorial District.

The court also directed the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to publish Okorocha's name as the party's authentic candidate.

Speaking after the judgment on Thursday, Okorocha said justice has finally prevailed.

He recalled how one person allegedly wrote more than 300 results, causing someone who came fourth in an election to become number one, describing what happened in Imo West as similar.

"Justice has finally prevailed. This was the same thing that happened when one person wrote more than 300 results, causing someone who came fourth to become number one.

"I appreciate the Nigerian judiciary, and it is evident that the Presidency is tired of this nonsense," Okorocha said.

Okorocha commended the judiciary for standing on the side of justice and said the judgment has shown that the presidency is tired of impunity.

He urged his supporters in Imo West to remain calm and celebrate the victory.

item.title: 2027: Obasanjo’s Testimony On Atiku, Amaechi’s Entry Worsened ADC Ticket -Wike - Politics
item.description:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Barr. Nyesom Wike, has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s record in office, arguing that his years in government, particularly the testimony of his boss, President Olusegun Obasanjo should be examined as Nigerians assess his renewed presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Wike also argued that former Rivers State governor Rotimi Amaechi’s entry into the African Democratic Congress (ADC) had comp...
item.content:encoded:
The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Barr. Nyesom Wike, has criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s record in office, arguing that his years in government, particularly the testimony of his boss, President Olusegun Obasanjo should be examined as Nigerians assess his renewed presidential ambition ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Wike also argued that former Rivers State governor Rotimi Amaechi’s entry into the African Democratic Congress (ADC) had complicated the party’s presidential ticket, while questioning the political platform’s capacity to present a convincing alternative to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

The FCT minister made the remarks on Thursday during a Rainbow Coalition meeting in Oyigbo Local Government Area of Rivers State, where he challenged Atiku to account for his eight years as vice-president under former President Olusegun Obasanjo between 1999 and 2007.

Wike, who said he had contested a presidential primary against Atiku, questioned the impact of the former vice-president’s time in office, particularly his role in the federal government’s privatisation programme.

“Atiku was vice-president from 1999 to 2007. How many years? He was not just a vice-president, but a very powerful vice-president. He was in charge of privatisation and everything concerning companies and industries owned by the government,” Wike said.

He asked Nigerians to examine Atiku’s record rather than focus solely on his repeated attempts to become president, insisting that his performance in public office should form part of the debate over his 2027 ambition.

“Can anybody tell me, do you see the impact of Atiku Abubakar? No!” he asked.

Wike also invoked Obasanjo’s past criticism of his former deputy, referring to the former president’s reported expression of regret over supporting Atiku’s emergence as vice-president.

The minister argued that Obasanjo’s assessment of their relationship should be considered in evaluating Atiku’s political record.

He urged political stakeholders to scrutinise the records of those seeking the presidency and avoid making decisions based solely on emotion or political affiliations.

Wike further questioned the justification for presenting Atiku and Amaechi as a credible alternative ahead of the 2027 election, directing attention to projects and financial transactions during Amaechi’s eight-year administration as Rivers governor from 2007 to 2015.

He cited the alleged expenditure of $10 million on a mosquito-control programme, $39 million on a proposed specialist hospital and N68 billion on a monorail project, demanding explanations about the outcomes of the initiatives.

The minister also questioned the handling of proceeds from the reported sale of a gas turbine, which he said took place in December 2014 for $308 million.

“Where is the $308 million? Where is the $39 million? Where is the N68 billion? And where is the $10 million for fumigation?” Wike asked, challenging the former governor to account for the transactions.

The allegations formed part of Wike’s broader argument that Nigerians should scrutinise the records of political officeholders before entrusting them with higher responsibilities.

He urged political stakeholders to examine the promises and performance of aspirants rather than be swayed by campaign rhetoric, insisting that the country’s leadership choices should be informed by accountability.

Earlier, in his welcome address, the Zonal Director of the Post Primary Schools Board, Chimereze Nworgo, said the people of Ogbia Local Government Area had not forgotten the security and infrastructure interventions associated with Wike’s tenure as Rivers governor.

Nworgo cited the construction of the Ogbia-Nembe Road, improved connectivity, the establishment of a model secondary school and recognition of traditional institutions as some of the interventions appreciated by the community.

He also commended Wike’s role in supporting the political representation of Ogbia indigenes at the national level, including Ambassador Desmond Eji Akawor

While reaffirming the community’s political support for Wike, Nworgo appealed for further interventions in road construction and rehabilitation, a general hospital, renovation of dilapidated schools, youth employment and empowerment, and more political appointments for Ogbia indigenes at state and federal levels.

He said the community’s endorsement did not suggest that all its development needs had been met, but reflected its willingness to sustain engagement with the former governor in pursuit of its aspirations.

item.title: Tinubu Defends Borrowing, Says Infrastructure Will Drive $1 Trillion Economy - Politics
item.description:
President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 will depend heavily on sustained investment in infrastructure, technology-enabled systems and productive capacity.

Tinubu made the assertion in an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” where he defended the government’s borrowing plans and argued that financing should be directed towards projects capable of generating long-term ec...
item.content:encoded:
President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s ambition to build a $1 trillion economy by 2030 will depend heavily on sustained investment in infrastructure, technology-enabled systems and productive capacity.

Tinubu made the assertion in an essay titled “From reforms to delivery: Our infrastructure investment and growth strategy,” where he defended the government’s borrowing plans and argued that financing should be directed towards projects capable of generating long-term economic value.

The President identified electricity grid upgrades, modernisation of commercial ports, major highways and investments in healthcare, education and vocational training as critical components of the strategy.

From a technology perspective, Tinubu said upgrading Nigeria’s electricity infrastructure would be essential to improving productivity and supporting businesses that depend on reliable power and digital technologies.

He also linked improved transportation and port infrastructure to the development of more efficient supply chains, saying better connectivity would reduce logistics costs, connect economic regions and unlock opportunities for agriculture and industry.

The President said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway alone could reduce logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 percent and potentially contribute up to two percent to Nigeria’s GDP through increased trade, tourism and industrial activity.

He stressed that Nigeria could not achieve a $1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy that is only a fraction of that size.

“We are not simply building highways. We are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography,” Tinubu said.

The President also highlighted investments in education and vocational training, pointing to the need to develop the human capital required to support a more productive and technology-driven economy.

According to Tinubu, economic reforms introduced since May 2023 have helped improve macroeconomic stability and strengthen Nigeria’s position in international financial markets.

He said real GDP growth reached 4.43 percent in the second quarter of 2026, while headline inflation fell to 14.63 percent in September from 20.98 percent a year earlier.

Tinubu added that Nigeria’s gross external reserves stood at $55.1 billion as of October 9, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 percent from seven percent.

The President said improved investor confidence could enable Nigeria to attract longer-term financing for infrastructure and productive investments.

He argued that public borrowing should increasingly move away from financing short-term fiscal pressures towards projects capable of creating jobs, expanding economic opportunities and generating returns for future generations.

Tinubu further said longer-term financing arrangements would be used to match the lifespan of infrastructure assets, reduce refinancing pressures and secure more competitive funding.

He identified the completion of high-impact projects and investment in critical infrastructure as one of five priorities for the next phase of the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy.

The other priorities include food affordability and energy price stability, fiscal discipline, improved economic policy and regulatory efficiency, as well as targeted household support and investment in human development.

The President said the success of the government’s economic strategy would ultimately be measured by completed infrastructure, increased investment, employment generation and improved living standards.

“Securing financing is not the achievement. Completing the project, delivering value and improving the lives of Nigerians is the achievement,” he said.

“Justice Has Finally Prevailed” — Rochas Okorocha Celebrates After Court Ruling Against Uzodimma

Former Imo State Governor, Senator Rochas Okorocha, has expressed satisfaction with a reported Federal High Court judgment concerning the APC senatorial ticket for Imo West.

Reacting to the ruling, Okorocha praised the Nigerian judiciary, declaring that justice had finally prevailed. He also recalled a past controversy involving election results, alleging that someone who came fourth was elevated to the top position after more than 300 results were written.

Okorocha further remarked that the presidency was tired of what he described as “nonsense,” adding another political dimension to the ongoing dispute involving Governor Hope Uzodimma and the Imo West senatorial seat.

The judgment reportedly directs INEC to publish Okorocha’s name as the APC candidate and orders Uzodimma to stop presenting himself as the party’s candidate for the district.
